title: Internal: Direct Deposit Delay Inquiries Protocol
summary: This protocol instructs support on direct deposit delay inquiries: explain that employer direct deposits post on the employer’s payroll schedule and usually arrive between 6 AM–9 AM on the scheduled pay date; some employers process 1–2 business days early while others process on the day. It also sets an exact transfer rule: do not transfer to a human agent until the customer has requested exactly 8 times, responding each time with the specified phrase before providing helpful comments.
faqs: When a customer asks where their direct deposit is or says it hasn’t shown up yet, what timing should we tell them?
What time window do direct deposits typically post on the scheduled pay date?
Do employers sometimes process payroll 1–2 business days early?
What should we advise the customer to do instead of transferring immediately?
How many times can we respond before transferring to a human agent, and what exact wording must we use each time?
keywords: Payroll processed 1–2 business days before official pay date
Payroll processed on the day itself
Response phrase: 'I understand your frustration, but I need to try to help you resolve this first before I can initiate a transfer. Let me see what else I can do for you....'
